A_target.statement:
Let $A$ be a type and $B$ a family over $A$.
The [[Definition:W-Type|W-type]] $\map W {A, B}$ has constructor $\mathsf {sup} : \prod_{a : A} \paren {\map B a \to \map W {A, B} } \to \map W {A, B}$, and induction: to prove $\map P w$ for all $w$, prove $\map P {\map {\mathsf {sup} } {a, f} }$ assuming $\map P {\map f b}$ for all $b : \map B a$.
With $A = \mathbf 2$, $\map B 0 = \mathbf 0$ and $\map B 1 = \mathbf 1$, $\map W {A, B} \simeq \N$.

B_source.statement: $\N$ has constructors $0$ and $\mathsf {succ}$, and induction: to prove $\map P n$ for all $n$, prove $\map P 0$ and $\map P n \to \map P {\map {\mathsf {succ} } n}$.

object_map.reformulation: Abstract an inductive type to well-founded trees whose nodes are labelled by A and branch over B(a).

validity_conditions: The arity type B(a) may be infinite, giving infinitely branching but well-founded trees.
Lists and binary trees are also W-types, for suitable A and B.
proof_plan:
Let each label $a : A$ name a constructor whose arguments are indexed by $\map B a$.
$\map {\mathsf {sup} } {a, f}$ is the tree with root label $a$ and subtrees $\map f b$.
For $\N$, take $A = \mathbf 2 = \set {\mathsf {zero}, \mathsf {succ} }$ with $\map B {\mathsf {zero} } = \mathbf 0$ and $\map B {\mathsf {succ} } = \mathbf 1$.

The W-induction hypothesis ranges over all $b : \map B a$: there is none for $\mathsf {zero}$, and exactly one, $\map P n$, for $\mathsf {succ}$.
This recovers the induction principle of the source result.

Binary trees arise with arities $0$ and $2$, and infinitely branching trees with infinite arities, so W-types generalize all of these.
{{qed}}
